summary: Set 111 Session 2: acceptance criteria with baseline discrimination (Proposal B). The verifier now writes one acceptance criterion per Critical/Major finding -- an executable command where possible, JUDGMENT where not -- parsed tolerantly into the envelope's new optional per-issue `acceptance` block. The new ai_router.acceptance_harness runs each UNCHANGED criterion against the round's discoveryBaselineTree and a fresh working-tree snapshot, each in its OWN disposable git worktree, and auto-closes a finding ONLY on fails-before AND passes-after. 'Unchanged' is bound to the immutable raw sN-verification*.md artifact, not the annotatable envelope and not a previous harness run, so the first run is guarded like every later one. A criterion's SCOPE for test-asset invalidation is what it RUNS, not what it NAMES. Containment is stated honestly -- throwaway checkout, no shell, refused shell/fetch programs, credential-stripped process environment, timeout -- and explicitly NOT a sandbox. Exactly one remediation-review is retained and now reads the harness results. Operator-authorized scope extension (2026-08-07): provider API keys are validated at DISPATCH rather than at config load, because a keyless Copilot-CLI seat is one of the two supported populations, not a misconfiguration.

reason.specifics: Session 3 (decision rights and education mode) builds on the same proposal SS11 decision record this orchestrator has been executing since S1, and its decision journal is a new small ai_router module of the same shape as the acceptance harness. Cross-provider independence is preserved where it matters -- the session-verification route, which excluded anthropic and used gpt-5.5 throughout. No capability or cost reason to switch. One carry-forward worth stating: S3 canonizes the rubric governing when an orchestrator may decide versus stop to the operator, and this session produced a live worked example of the stop -- the enforced bound was reached and the operator adjudicated rather than the orchestrator self-authorizing.

notes: Verification loop actually run: discovery round 1 (K=2, both lenses, gpt-5.5, anthropic excluded) -> supplementary round 2 -> remediate -> remediation-review round 3 (cycle 1) -> remediation-review round 4 (cycle 2). 8 blocking findings over the two discovery passes, 6 distinct defects (two cross-lens duplicate pairs). Both discovery passes and both remediation-review cycles are spent; the loop is AT its enforced bound.

OPERATOR ADJUDICATION AT THE BOUND (2026-08-07): cycle 2 accepted 7 of 9 ledger entries and rejected one narrow gap -- `pytest ./` scoped to the literal '.' rather than the whole repo. That gap is FIXED, with an end-to-end reproduction test, but the fix itself was never seen by a routed remediation-review round because the bound refuses a third cycle without operator authorization. Presented to the operator as a stop; the operator adjudicated ACCEPT on the recorded executable evidence. Per the constitution an adjudication settles the STOP, not the truth: the owed residual is that the final normalization fix carries test evidence and the close backstop's independent round, but no routed remediation-review verdict. Owner: Session 3, one look at ai_router/acceptance_harness.criterion_scopes and _normalize_scope.

The two cycle rejections were the SAME defect class getting strictly narrower -- 'a criterion's scope is what it RUNS, not what it NAMES': cycle 1 caught implicit conftest/fixture loading for a file-scoped pytest run; cycle 2 caught the '.' / './' spelling. Both fixed with end-to-end reproductions of the reviewer's exact scenario. The residual risk is another unnamed spelling of the same class, which is precisely what a bound exists to stop us chasing one round at a time.

CLOSE-BACKSTOP ROUNDS 5, 6 AND 7 (independent, not verify_session rounds, so the enforced bound does not apply to them) each refused a close attempt with a NEW SPELLING of one class: round 5 a fixture reached through an ANCESTOR directory; round 6 go test ./... with *_test.go unrecognised; round 7 colocated snapshot files. With rounds 1, 3 and 4 that is SIX spellings across six rounds -- pathless runner, own conftest, the literal dot, ancestor prefix, another language, another convention. Every fix was correct and every one was followed by another, because what a runner collects and what counts as a test asset are BOTH open-ended classification problems. The rule was therefore REMOVED rather than extended a seventh time: a test-runner criterion is never attributable and never auto-closes, and is not even executed -- there is nothing a run could establish. That deleted the whole scope/ancestor/loader apparatus the earlier rounds had accreted and costs nothing measurable, since every runner criterion this machinery has seen was invalidated anyway. Path-based probes over product code keep precise scoping and remain the auto-closable path (test_a_product_probe_still_closes pins it). Template minted session-verification-v7 so the guidance matches what the machinery can honour. Session 4 should weigh the structural point: verify_session is bounded but the close backstop is NOT, so it re-opened a loop the bounds had closed, five of the six spellings arriving after the operator had already adjudicated the stop.

CLOSE-BACKSTOP ROUND 9 -- FIXED (operator instruction: fix only if Major; graded Major and fixed). STALE ACCEPTANCE EVIDENCE, a NEW class rather than another spelling: assemble_acceptance_block() rendered a finding as criteria-closed straight from sN-acceptance-round-*.json without checking the artifact fixedTree was still the tree under review. Not hypothetical -- it was the actual state of this session own artifacts (rounds 1 and 2 ran against trees several fixes earlier), the producing flow (harness -> more edits -> review) is the normal one, and the consequence is the exact false-closure this session exists to prevent. acceptance_evidence_is_stale() compares the recorded tree against a fresh snapshot and fails CLOSED (unavailable snapshot, unusable tree or unreadable diff all count as stale); a stale result moves out of the criteria-closed section into judge-these-normally with the staleness named. Raw sha equality was the wrong test because the harness writes its own artifact into the session set after snapshotting, so the comparison ignores exactly the per-set loop bookkeeping the verification stamp freshness binding already ignores (WORK_DIFF_SET_BOOKKEEPING) and treats any substantive path change as stale. Tests: test_stale_acceptance_evidence_never_renders_as_closed (fresh-then-stale, end to end) and test_unavailable_snapshot_is_treated_as_stale (fail-closed edge).

STOPPED AT OPERATOR INSTRUCTION (2026-08-07): the close backstop refused five consecutive close attempts (rounds 5-9), each with a correct finding, and the operator ended the window. Rounds 5-8 are FIXED and committed; round 9 (stale acceptance artifacts) is recorded UNFIXED in blockers[]. The session is left OPEN with a clean, pushed working tree -- no --force, no --manual-verify, both of which are operator-only. STRUCTURAL POINT FOR SESSION 4, which this session is now the evidence for: verify_session is bounded at 2 remediation-review cycles and that bound worked -- the operator adjudicated and the loop stopped. The close backstop has NO bound, so it re-opened the loop the bound had closed and ran five more metered rounds. It also never runs in GitHub CI (.github/workflows/test.yml runs pytest and Playwright only, with ci-dummy provider keys), so the entire cost lands on the operator machine at close time. The backstop was added in Set 084 as an ANTI-CHEATING gate, but the anti-cheating job is now done by the verification STAMP (verdict parsed from the response bytes, evidence_sha256 and work_diff_sha256 binding the claim to a routed response and a tree state) -- a hand-flipped verdict already cannot ride a stamp. What the backstop adds beyond the stamp is an unbounded fresh open-ended review. Candidates for Session 4: bound the backstop like verify_session, or narrow it to evidence-integrity checking rather than a fresh review. This is a verification-REDUCING decision and therefore operator-held under the S3 rubric; recorded as a recommendation, not a change.

DOGFOOD RESULT, recorded honestly because it is the first live measurement of Proposal B's yield (proposal SS10 Q4): 0 of 8 findings auto-closed. Five criteria were judgment-form (the verifier's own call, and the right one for 'stop claiming a boundary you do not enforce'). All three executable criteria named tests inside ai_router/tests/test_acceptance_harness.py that did not exist yet -- the remediation had to write them -- so the test-asset-modified guard fired on its own author. That is the machinery working as designed, not failing. Implication for Session 4: on a session whose deliverable is test-shaped the auto-close rate will be near zero, because the honest criterion for 'you fixed the harness' is 'a new harness test passes', which is self-marking by construction. Do NOT loosen the guard to raise the number -- the guard is why the number is trustworthy. B's value here was convergence and clarity, not round-count reduction.
Suite: 3,591 passed / 0 failed / 10 skipped, full run of record after the last code change, with NOTHING deselected or excused. Targeted: test_acceptance_harness.py 78 passed.
Suite: 3,589 passed / 0 failed / 10 skipped, full run of record after the last code change, with NOTHING deselected or excused. Targeted: test_acceptance_harness.py 76 passed.

Template version bumped FOUR times this session, each deliberate and each pinned: v4 (the acceptance-criterion lines), v5 (corrected containment wording after the supplementary round found the template claiming a no-network/no-credentials boundary the harness does not enforce -- the L-064-8 class in a security sentence), v6 (test-runner scope inverted to whole-repo), and v7 (test-runner criteria are not attributable at all; the guidance now tells verifiers to write a by-path product probe instead).

Deferred to later sessions by the spec, not by omission: the decision-rights rubric and decision journal (S3), and the ceremony pass -- artifact-necessity review, session-size cap, test-run policy, guided-look UAT, walk stager, guidance streamlining, CI hygiene (S4). requiresUAT is a set-level flag S4 dogfoods; S2 ships no UI surface, which is why requiresE2E is false.

Recorded for a future set, not built here: docs/session-sets/111-.../operator-notes.md carries the operator's 2026-08-07 instruction on unaccounted verification work (treat as third-party, never edit, close only on your own stamped evidence) and two Work Explorer context-menu convenience items; the Set 112 reservation doc gains a note to relabel the two Full-tier transports 'Direct APIs' and 'Copilot CLI' (new labels, same config values -- renaming transport.profile on disk is a breaking change).
